doc.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: 'A Love Supreme', faith and belief in the notes
summary: Talk of Coltrane announcing intent, and Harrison's statement that he believes his notes will take care of him.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: You just made me think of something that I should have thought of many years ago. If he spoke on it. And I wonder now if the “Love Supreme” record reached so many people because he announced his intention.

But the supreme to you, what does that mean? It might be — your supreme might be different from my supreme, based on our experience, based on our knowledge of, based on our knowledge, and intellect and intuition, intuition, intuition. There’s a lot of stuff we believe in that we can’t really see. We have faith. Faith is belief. We believe in something. It might not be manifested physically but we believe in it. That’s very important as a musician. You know. I believe these notes is going to take care of me, you know what I mean?
Can you say that again? © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
I believe these notes that I produce is going to take care of me. You know, and I have to make sure of that.
